clue.text: Composer's endearing Welsh appellation

definitions.meaning: Johann Sebastian, the German Baroque master of the fugue
in Wales the word is used like 'dear' or 'love' when addressing someone

explanation.surface: A Welsh nickname of affection for a great composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The German composer shares his surname with the Welsh term of affection meaning little one or dear.

clue.text: Walk in London, one with plenty of bars with high-fliers inside

definitions.meaning: a street beside St James's Park in London, named after a royal aviary

definitions.text: one with plenty of bars with high-fliers inside
definitions.meaning: a cage with many bars holding birds, the high-fliers

explanation.surface: A London street with many pubs full of high achievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' and 'high-fliers' suggest pubs and successful people; they are cage bars and birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdcage Walk is a street in Westminster; a cage for pet birds has many wire bars.

clue.text: Clothes dropped by actors half in the wings

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word for being in the wings is kept

parts.note: an actor waiting in the wings is offstage

explanation.surface: Theatre costumes discarded by actors waiting in the wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-offs are garments discarded by their owner, often handed on to others.

clue.text: Case revealing jealousy

definitions.meaning: a grammatical case, the one showing ownership, as in 'my' or 'John's'
showing a jealous desire to keep someone to oneself

explanation.surface: Evidence in a dispute that shows someone was jealous.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names the genitive form of a noun as one case; a clingy, jealous partner is described by the same adjective.

clue.text: Old part of mansion's down

parts.note: a wing is a section of a large house

explanation.surface: An old wing of a stately home has fallen down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a direction or fallen; it means in debt, as in being twenty pounds down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down by a sum means it is still owed, unpaid debt.

clue.text: No solid grounding for these arty-crafty views

definitions.text: No solid grounding for these arty-crafty views

parts.words: No solid grounding for these arty-crafty views
parts.note: sounds like a jibe at artistic opinions with no basis, but describes pictures showing water rather than land

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing some arty opinions as baseless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'views' suggests opinions and 'grounding' a basis for them; really these are pictures of the ocean, with no land in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine paintings depict the ocean, so their scenes have no dry land underneath.

clue.text: Country garden known to American detectives

parts.note: Scotland is a country of the UK
Americans call a garden a yard

explanation.surface: A country garden familiar to visiting American sleuths.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOTLAND YARD is the London headquarters of the Metropolitan Police, and the name is used for its detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Met's headquarters gives its name to the force's investigating officers collectively.

clue.text: Reptiles head off antelopes

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed from the reptile word

parts.note: lizards are reptiles

explanation.surface: Reptiles bite the heads off antelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: The izard is the Pyrenean chamois, a goat-antelope of southern European mountains.

clue.text: Coming in to fish, person's picked up protective coat

indicators.note: coming in to means entering, so one piece goes inside the fish

parts.note: an eel is a fish

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a man is a person; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Someone wades in to land a fish and picks up a waterproof coat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'picked up' means read upwards, so the person is turned round before 'Coming in to' puts it inside the fish. 'Coat' suggests clothing; it is a layer of paint or glaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard glossy surface layer, such as paint or the coating on teeth.

clue.text: Biscuit that ends up in Bristol channel

definitions.meaning: a hard dry baked biscuit, often given to teething babies

definitions.text: that ends up in Bristol channel
definitions.meaning: the River Usk, written ..., flows out into the Severn estuary and the Bristol Channel

explanation.surface: A biscuit dropped overboard drifts out to sea off Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: the Welsh River Usk, abbreviated R. USK, is something that ends up in the Bristol Channel, the inlet between south Wales and south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusk is a twice-baked dry biscuit; the river Usk, written with R for river, drains into that channel.

clue.text: Make a pass at woman after a lot of beer and a cocktail

indicators.note: after puts the woman and pass pieces behind the beer piece
a lot of something is most of it but not all, so the last letter of the beer word is dropped

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
a col is a mountain pass
Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man flirts with a woman after a few beers and a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a pass' looks like one idea, flirting, but 'pass' alone is COL; 'a lot of' drops the last letter of PINT to give PIN. 'Make', 'at' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A piña colada is a rum, coconut and pineapple mixed drink, a classic example of the category.

clue.text: Blurts out secrets — shocks with the pronounced indiscretion

parts.note: blows are shocks, setbacks

indicators.note: pronounced means the next word is replaced by one said the same

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

explanation.surface: A tactless person reveals secrets, causing shocks with an obvious blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' reads as 'marked'; it signals that GAFFE is swapped for the same-sounding GAFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing the gaff is an idiom for revealing a plot or secret.

clue.text: To be pedantic about work record is smart

indicators.note: about here means one word goes round the others, wrapping them

parts.note: chic means smart, stylish
op is short for opus, a work
a log is a written record, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: Someone fussing over a work record that seems tidy and smart.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop logic is an idiom for arguing over fine distinctions in a hair-splitting way.

clue.text: Youngster given extremely large spoon

parts.note: a lad is a young boy

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters, the first and last, of the following word

explanation.surface: A child handed a huge spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladle is a deep long-handled serving spoon used for soup.

clue.text: Giving attractive coverage in paper, for the present

definitions.text: Giving attractive coverage in paper, for the present

parts.words: Giving attractive coverage in paper, for the present
parts.note: reads like a newspaper giving favourable press coverage for now, but describes decorating a gift in pretty paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper giving someone flattering coverage, at least for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coverage in paper' suggests journalism and 'for the present' suggests 'for now'; both really point to wrapping a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative paper put round a gift makes it attractive; this phrase names that wrapping activity.

clue.text: In large tract of land, right time to transplant herbaceous plant

indicators.note: in means these pieces are placed within the land mass

parts.note: Asia is a vast continent

indicators.note: to transplant means to move, so the letters of time are shifted around

explanation.surface: In a vast region of land, the right moment to replant a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to transplant' gives TEMI from the clue's time word; 'In' puts R and those letters inside the continent, straight after its first letter. 'Plant' in the surface and the definition is a neat double use of the gardening picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic plants including wormwood and mugwort.

clue.text: Part of Eucharist where old boy finds nothing in traditional language

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: in means the nothing piece goes inside the language word

parts.note: Latin was the traditional language of the Catholic Mass
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: In a church service, an ex-pupil finds no Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The oblation is the offering of bread and wine to God at the Mass.

clue.text: Running away is appropriate, having pocketed pounds

indicators.note: having pocketed means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: fitting means appropriate, suitable
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Fleeing is quite right once you have pocketed the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Flitting is chiefly British and Scottish usage for moving house or departing hastily, as in doing a moonlight flit.
explanation.definitionFit: To flit is to depart suddenly, often secretly to dodge debts.

clue.text: Standing to sound percussion instrument as a show of one's power

parts.note: status is one's standing or rank

indicators.note: to sound like means the next word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: a cymbal is a brass percussion plate

explanation.surface: Banging a drum or cymbal to show off one's power and standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A prestige possession such as a fancy car is displayed to advertise wealth and rank.

clue.text: Plane changing course maybe for one providing cash

definitions.meaning: an aircraft tilts sideways to turn, so a plane turning does this
a person who runs or works in a financial institution

explanation.surface: A plane turning round may be carrying someone with funds.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft tilts or banks when turning; a financier who runs a bank also shares the name.

clue.text: Enthusiast wants to eat, avoiding a self-service place

parts.note: a buff is a keen fan, as in a film buff

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, so the letter is dropped from the eating word

explanation.surface: A keen fan wants to eat but avoids a self-service restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet is a meal or counter where diners serve themselves.

clue.text: Presumably returning a little interest

indicators.note: returning means the letters taken are read backwards, right to left
a little of the word Presumably means only part of it is used

explanation.surface: A guess that a small amount of interest is coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes ESUMA from inside PRESUMABLY and 'returning' turns it round. 'Interest' wants to be bank interest; it is the verb, to entertain.
explanation.definitionFit: To interest someone is to hold their attention, close to entertaining or diverting them.

clue.text: Offender, as intended, is caught and run in

indicators.note: in means the following pieces are placed inside the intended word

parts.note: meant means as intended, deliberately
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An offender, just as planned, is caught and brought in by police.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or villain, someone who breaks rules.

clue.text: Blade son takes to dispatch weak animal

parts.note: to cull is to kill off the weakest members of a herd

explanation.surface: A son takes a knife to kill a weak animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade' suggests a knife; it is an oar's blade, or the oar itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A scull is a single oar for rowing, whose flat end is the blade.

clue.text: Nightmarish extremes of funk in terrible sea-quake

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other
terrible signals the following word is wrecked and rearranged
extremes of means the first and last letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A nightmarish fear at the edge of a terrible earthquake under the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the letters of the quake word, and 'in' places the outer letters of 'funk' in the gap after its first two letters. The answer derives from Franz Kafka, the Prague novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Kafka's novels portray surreal, oppressive bureaucratic dread, so the adjective describes nightmarish situations.

clue.text: Rugby country where three characters get points in one case

definitions.text: Rugby country where three characters get points in one case

parts.words: Rugby country where three characters get points in one case
parts.note: a Pacific rugby nation whose name, written in lower case, has three letters carrying dots above them

explanation.surface: A rugby nation where three players score points in a single match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' and 'case' suggest scoring and a court case; really, written in lower case, the name has two i's and a j, three letters topped with a dot.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiji is a South Pacific island nation famous for its rugby union and sevens teams.

clue.text: Facing endorsement after alibi is exploded

indicators.note: an alibi exploded is one blown apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Approval comes once an alibi has been exposed as false.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of formal approval, such as a treaty, is awaiting endorsement.

clue.text: Disadvantage of two whitish metals together

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin, a silvery-white metal
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: The drawback of a pair of pale metals combined.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden drawback or problem.
